Freebuff on Omarchy

Freebuff is a free, ad-supported AI coding agent for the terminal: no API key, no card, no subscription, with the model bill paid by text ads shown while the agent works.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add freebuff
cd ~/my-project
freebuff

That installs Freebuff v0.2.36-1 (49.3 MB download, 137.7 MB installed, depends on glibc). Then describe what you want in plain language. Freebuff finds the relevant files, makes the changes, and runs the checks that matter for your project.

Getting started (5 minutes)

1. Launch it in a project.

Change into a project directory and run freebuff. There is no API key step and no credit card screen. First launch drops you into an interactive terminal UI where you type tasks, not commands.

2. The 3 things you need to know:

  • Start small. Ask it to explain one file first, then ask it to fix one small bug. Watch what it changes before handing it a large task. The agent plans the work, edits files, runs commands, and reports back.
  • Pick your model with /model. The picker shows each model’s hourly Freebucks rate before you start. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the default workhorse; the free experimental models (Beam 1.0, Glyph Cluster, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning) use none of your daily hours. Stronger models (GPT-6 Luna, Muse Spark 1.3, Claude Haiku 5.5) sit behind paid plans.
  • Set project rules in AGENTS.md. Freebuff reads AGENTS.md from the project root at the start of each chat and falls back to CLAUDE.md if there is no AGENTS.md. Put your conventions there once instead of repeating them in every prompt.

3. Config location.

Per-project config lives in the project itself: AGENTS.md for instructions, .agents/mcp.json for MCP servers, .agents/skills for skills, and chats stored locally per project. A global config path is not confirmed from the docs — if you find one on your machine, that’s the gap this guide still needs verified.

Practical notes: Your chats stay local and resumable — run freebuff --continue to reopen your last chat, and /export to save a Markdown transcript. MCP servers load from .agents/mcp.json in the standard mcpServers format, and skills in .agents/skills (or .claude/skills) appear as /skill:<name> commands.

Common issues & fixes

Your daily allowance runs out mid-task

Freebuff meters use in Freebucks, not dollars: every account gets 100 per day, refilled at midnight Pacific, and unused credits do not roll over. A session runs about an hour and is charged at the selected model’s hourly rate, shown in the /model picker.

Fix: Switch to a cheaper model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Slow uses one hour of balance per hour of use) or to a free experimental model that uses no hours, or wait for the midnight refill. Referrals and bounties earn extra hours on top of the free daily allowance. (Freebuff README; freebuff.com)

You only see a few models, or the allowance is much smaller than advertised (limited access mode)

Model access depends on your country, and a VPN can trigger it too. Full access covers 25 or more countries; outside those, Freebuff drops to limited mode with only DeepSeek V4.1 Flash models and a 5-hour daily allowance (4 hours on a VPN or proxy).

Fix: Connect directly without a VPN. A paid plan adds more models and hours. (Freebuff README; dev.to walkthrough)

Text ads appear in your terminal, and you are unsure what happens to your code

This is the deal, not a bug: text ads pay for the models. Ads sit in a box marked Ad between agent turns and never appear inside generated code. The README is upfront that messages, traces, and files may be analyzed to personalize ads and train ad models, and some models may use data for training.

Fix: The model picker flags those models, so pick one without that note before pointing the agent at private code. Project files are not sent to advertising providers. (Freebuff README)

You try to run Freebuff in a script or CI pipeline and it does nothing useful

The CLI is interactive only; there is no headless mode.

Fix: Use it in a live terminal session. For scripted or CI runs, use an agent built for that, such as Kilo Code CLI (kilo run --auto) or Kimi Code CLI (kimi -p). (freebuff.com)

A model you read about is gone from the picker, or a strong model stops after one session a day

The catalog changes often and the README deliberately does not list prices: models get retired (GLM 5.3 Flash, MiMo 2.6 Pro, Gemini 3.8 Flash and others have already left the catalog) and some are capped (GPT-6.1 Sol is limited to one session per day for every account, paid plans included).

Fix: Trust the picker, not a blog post: it shows the current catalog, each model’s hourly rate, and any session cap before you start. (Freebuff README)

Verdict: If you want a coding agent right now with no key, no card, and no config, Freebuff is the lowest-friction way in. If the ads or the daily cap start to hurt, Kilo Code CLI is the natural next step, since it keeps the terminal workflow and lets you bring your own model.

Freebuff is a free alternative to Claude Code ($20/mo)

Freebuff is a free alternative to Claude Code (Pro $20/mo). What you give up: an ad-free screen, unlimited usage, headless and CI runs, and the top Claude models on the free tier. What you keep: multi-agent coding, file editing, command running, MCP servers, skills, and AGENTS.md project rules, for $0. Freebuff’s own comparison puts rival coding agents at $120 to $1,200 a year against its $0. The honest version: the software and the models are free because advertisers pay, and the price is a daily allowance plus inline ads. Paid plans (Starter $8/mo, Plus $25/mo, Pro $60/mo, checked November 2026) buy more hours and stronger models if the free tier runs short.

How to switch from Claude Code (~15 minutes per project)

  1. Export from Claude Code: there is no export step. Your project instructions already live in CLAUDE.md, and Freebuff reads that file as a fallback when no AGENTS.md exists.
  2. Import into Freebuff: copy CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md in the project root if you want it picked up first. Move MCP servers from your Claude config into .agents/mcp.json in the standard mcpServers format, and skills from .claude/skills into .agents/skills. Chats do not transfer; start fresh.
  3. Install Freebuff on Omarchy: omarchy pkg add freebuff.
  4. What doesn’t transfer: chat history, Claude Code’s headless and CI workflows (Freebuff is interactive only), and access to Claude models on the free tier.

Frequently asked questions

Is Freebuff really free?

Yes. No subscription, no credits to buy, no API key, no credit card. Text ads shown in the terminal pay the model costs, and every account gets 100 Freebucks a day, refilled at midnight Pacific. Paid plans exist for more hours and stronger models, but the free tier is a real free tier, not a trial.

How does Freebuff make money?

Text ads. They appear in a box marked Ad in the terminal while the agent works. Your messages and usage may be analyzed to personalize ads and train ad models, and some models may use data for training, which the picker flags.

Do I need an API key or an account?

No API key and no card. The upstream install is npm install -g freebuff, then run freebuff in a project. Whether first launch on Omarchy asks for any login at all is still unverified.

Does Freebuff work offline or run a model locally?

No to both. The agent runs on your machine, but the models run in the cloud. Every prompt goes to a model provider.

Where does Freebuff store its config?

Per project: AGENTS.md for instructions, .agents/mcp.json for MCP servers, .agents/skills for skills, and chats stored locally per project. A global config path is not confirmed from the docs read for this guide.

Which models can I use for free?

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (the default), Solar Mini 4 and Solar Pro 4, plus the free experimental models Beam 1.0, Glyph Cluster, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, which use none of your daily hours. GPT-6 Luna, Muse Spark 1.3, Muse Ember, Claude Haiku 5.5, and GPT-6.1 Terra need a paid plan.
